requirements.statement: The live animals notification list stays where it is, at the live-animals set root in the animals frontend, and is reframed there to Design Release 2.1's category list, reading the animals backend's list; it is not moved to the INS frontend in this programme.
requirements.why: The afternoon rulings of 9 October keep each notification list in its own frontend and reframe it in place, built on the animals frontend and animals backend; this replaces, for this programme, the move to the INS frontend that the morning ruling had kept from Rhys's DR1 judgement (c-159).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-001 and repo-backend-p3-001 (proven by trace-e2e-p3-001): the list is already the animals frontend's GET route at the live-animals set root, backed by the animals backend's GET /notifications; what the page shows changes under the requirements that follow.

requirements.statement: The live animals list's browser title is 'Dashboard - Import notification service - GOV.UK', with the caption 'Dashboard' above an h1 naming the category, 'Live animals'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 titles every list 'Dashboard' and heads it with the category, so a trader can tell which category's notifications they are looking at; the 9 October afternoon ruling names this frame for the reframed list.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page title and the h1 are both 'Import notification service' (browser title 'Import notification service - Import notification service - GOV.UK'); the 'Dashboard' caption already exists.

requirements.statement: The list page has no introductory paragraph and no Messages link: the heading is followed directly by the 'Create new' button and, on the live animals and germinal products lists, the 'Use template' button. Plants' list loses its introductory paragraph in the same way.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's category list goes straight from its heading to its actions; plants takes the same frame in the same increment (9 October afternoon ruling, claim 55).
requirements.deltaNote: Today one paragraph about telling the authorities about imported live animals sits under the animals heading, and plants' dashboard has its own intro paragraph (its guidance-link sentence renders only when a guidance URL is supplied, and none is).

requirements.statement: The list page has a 'Back' link to the overall home.
requirements.why: Not built: the 9 October afternoon ruling sends every page Design Release 2.1 points at the overall dashboard to the set's own list, and has the INS front door reached through the service navigation as today, so the list, now the set's own landing page, carries no Back link (c-notification-list-001).

requirements.statement: The live animals list has a primary 'Create new' button that starts a live animals notification, carrying the list's category into the create journey, in place of today's 'Start a new notification' start button. Where it points and how the category is carried are the services' to name.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 starts a notification from 'Create new', carrying the category the trader was looking at; the 9 October rulings keep the destination and the category, not the prototype's create-notification?category= address (c-251), and name 'Create new' starting a notification as part of the reframed list's frame.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a GOV.UK start button 'Start a new notification' POSTs to /live-animals/notifications, which creates a draft and its reference on every press and redirects straight to its origin page.

requirements.statement: The live animals and germinal products lists have a secondary 'Use template' button beside 'Create new' that goes to the templates page, without a category. Plants' list has no 'Use template' button.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers starting from a saved template from every category list, and the templates ruling keeps the button out of the dashboard block; templates cover only the animals sets, and plants is left out of template mode until it has templates.

requirements.statement: The list page has an h2 'Summary' section with two glance cards: 'Action needed' with 'Tasks requiring your attention' and a 'View tasks' link to the action-needed page filtered to the category, and 'Status updated' with 'Changes in the past 24 hours' and a 'View updates' link to the changes page filtered to the category.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts what needs the trader's attention at the top of each category list; the 9 October afternoon ruling counts the list's Summary cards (inc-139) as the INS dashboard's summary information, blocked until its requirements firm up.
requirements.blockedBy: The INS dashboard's requirements firm up (Sam, 9 October): the counts, glance cards and drill-downs are summary information, re-distilled once those requirements exist.

requirements.statement: The list's 'Action needed' glance card shows a live count for the category: the notifications showing the 'Action required' tag (a 'Delayed' one does not count), matching the Action needed list its link opens.
requirements.why: The count is only useful if it agrees with the drill-down page; a notification is action-required when it is missing a required document or required identifiers, as Design Release 2.1 works it out (c-149). It is summary information, blocked with the Summary cards.
requirements.blockedBy: The INS dashboard's requirements firm up (Sam, 9 October): the glance-card counts are summary information, re-distilled once those requirements exist.

requirements.statement: The list's notifications sit under an h2 'Notifications', replacing the h2 'Your notifications', on the live animals list and on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 heads the list section 'Notifications'; DR1's 'My notifications' row was only deferred, never judged; plants takes the same frame.
requirements.deltaNote: Today both lists use the medium h2 'Your notifications' (Welsh 'Eich hysbysiadau'), which the animals frontend also uses as the breadcrumb label on the delete and cancel-amendment pages.

requirements.statement: On the live animals list the search, sort and additional filters sit in one column above the tabs inside the 'Notifications' section, with no 'Filter notifications' heading and no separate one-third filter aside beside the results.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lays the list out as one column: search and sort, then the filters disclosure, then the tabs and cards.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the list is two columns: a one-third aside headed 'Filter notifications' (h3) holding the search, and a two-thirds column holding the results count, sort and cards.

requirements.statement: The live animals list's search field is labelled 'Search by'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label; today's 'Keyword or reference' promises a keyword search the service does not give.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the field is labelled 'Keyword or reference' (small bold label) and named referenceNumber.

requirements.statement: The live animals list's search field has the hint 'Keyword, notification number, commodity, consignee or consignor'.
requirements.why: The hint tells the trader what the search matches.

requirements.statement: The live animals list's search is submitted by a real submit button that shows only a magnifying-glass icon and whose accessible name is 'Search'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's search control; the 9 October afternoon ruling lets the icon-only button stand as long as it is a real submit button of the GET form (c-notification-list-002).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the button is a standard primary GOV.UK button with the visible text 'Search'.

requirements.statement: A search on the live animals list lists the notifications whose reference number, commodity, consignee or consignor contains the searched text, ignoring case, rather than only an exact, whole reference number.
requirements.why: The hint promises a keyword search over those facts. The prototype cannot persist or query, so its search is inert; a real search box that does nothing would mislead the trader, so the real service applies it (c-162).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the term is passed to the listing only as referenceNumber, an exact match on a complete reference, so a commodity or a party name finds nothing.

requirements.statement: After a search the field keeps the searched text, and searching with an empty or whitespace-only field clears the search and lists everything again.
requirements.why: The trader can see and change what they searched for; both Design Release 2.1 and today keep the text.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-016 and repo-frontend-p3-015: the field is filled with the current term, and a blank or whitespace-only term means no filter (proven by repo-frontend-p3-114).

requirements.statement: On the live animals list, search, sort and every additional filter are one GET form to the list's own path, submitted by the search button; it carries the current tab (unless 'In progress') and the current page (when above 1) as hidden fields, so the result stays on that tab. Changing a select or a radio submits nothing by itself.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts sort and filters inside the search form with one submit control, and the 9 October afternoon ruling makes it one GET form whose submit button searches and sorts on the server, so the page works without JavaScript; today search and sort are two forms and a search always restarts at page 1.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the search form carries only the sort as a hidden field (no page, no tab), and the sort is a separate form.

requirements.statement: The live animals list's sort select is labelled 'Sort by:'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label for the sort control.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the select is labelled 'Sort by' with no colon (small bold label).

requirements.statement: The live animals list's sort select offers exactly 'Newest first', 'Oldest first' and 'Arrival date', in that order, with no unselected 'Select one' option.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's three orderings replace today's four; DR1 already rejected an unsorted 'Select one' state, so the list is always sorted.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the options are 'Arrival (newest to oldest)', 'Arrival (oldest to newest)', 'Date created (newest to oldest)' and 'Date created (oldest to newest)'.

requirements.statement: The live animals list is always sorted and the sort is applied for real: 'Newest first' and 'Oldest first' order by when the notification was created, 'Arrival date' orders by arrival date newest first, and with no sort chosen the list is ordered by arrival date newest first with 'Arrival date' selected.
requirements.why: DR1 judged the list always sorted; the prototype never orders its list, so the real service applies the orderings, keeping today's default order (which the prototype's completed tab also shows).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the default is 'Arrival (newest to oldest)' and any unknown value falls back to it; the stub orders every option by creation date, and no test proves the order of the cards.

requirements.statement: The live animals list has no 'Update sort' button: the chosen sort is applied by the search button with the rest of the form, and the chosen option stays selected after the page reloads.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's sort has no button of its own; DR1 only deferred this difference, and the 9 October afternoon ruling has one submit button for the whole form, with no select submitting on change.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a separate GET sort form with a secondary 'Update sort' button applies the sort, carrying the page and the search as hidden fields.

requirements.statement: The live animals list has an 'Additional filters' disclosure built from the GOV.UK details component inside the search form, closed on load and open whenever an arrival-date, date-range or status filter is set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps the extra filters out of the way until the trader needs them; the 9 October afternoon ruling builds the disclosure from GOV.UK details rather than the prototype's custom chevron markup (c-notification-list-002).

requirements.statement: The additional filters have a 'By arrival date' column of small GOV.UK radios 'Today', 'Tomorrow' and 'Next 7 days' (legend visually hidden, the same words shown as its heading); choosing one and searching lists only notifications arriving in that range, and the choice stays checked.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets a trader find what is arriving soon; the prototype's filter is inert, so the real service applies it.

requirements.statement: The additional filters have a 'By date range' column with the hint 'For example, 27/3/2026' and two MoJ date pickers, 'Start date' and 'End date' (a 'Choose date' calendar opening on the current month, weeks starting Monday, each a plain text field without JavaScript); the list shows only notifications arriving between the two dates, and the entered dates are kept.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's date range; it sits beside the arrival-date radios, so it filters the arrival date, as DR1's row also read it. The 9 October afternoon ruling accepts the MoJ date picker here, because the range is a search filter, not a date read from a document.

requirements.statement: When the start or end date cannot be read as a date, or the end date is before the start date, the list shows a GOV.UK error summary and an inline error on the date field ('Enter a real start date', 'Enter a real end date' or 'End date must be the same as or after the start date'), opens 'Additional filters', keeps the entered text in the 'Start date' and 'End date' pickers, and lists notifications without the date-range filter.
requirements.why: Validation is a real constraint the prototype cannot express, so a date the filter cannot use is answered with an error rather than silently ignored; the prototype still sets the labels and keeps the entered dates, and the GOV.UK date-input error pattern supplies the messages (c-166, which the 9 October afternoon ruling keeps).

requirements.statement: The additional filters have a 'Status' select offering exactly 'Select one', 'Action required', 'Submitted' and 'Completed'; choosing a status and searching lists only notifications in it, and the choice stays selected.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's status filter offers the statuses a trader acts on; drafts have their own tab, so Draft is not offered.

requirements.statement: The live animals list has three tabs, 'In progress', 'Draft' and 'Completed', built as MoJ sub navigation, each a link that loads the page with that tab chosen; 'In progress' is the list with no tab chosen, an unknown or missing tab shows 'In progress', and following a tab drops the search, sort and filters. The tab parameter's name and values are the animals frontend's.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 separates work in flight, unfinished drafts and finished notifications, and drafts keep a home on the list, which DR1 said must not be lost; the 9 October afternoon ruling builds the tabs as MoJ sub navigation on the animals frontend's own list, and the prototype never names query parameters (c-251).

requirements.statement: The 'In progress' tab lists submitted and action-required notifications, 'Draft' lists drafts and 'Completed' lists completed notifications.
requirements.why: Each tab holds the notifications at that stage, as Design Release 2.1 sets them out; a notification being amended goes in 'In progress' (c-165).

requirements.statement: A notification being amended is listed in the 'In progress' tab with today's yellow 'Amending' tag and its status-driven actions (Resume, Copy as new, Cancel amendment, Delete).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 has no amending state and its catch-all status mapping would file one as a draft only by fallback, while the backend persists an amendment as a submitted notification in AMEND that never returns to DRAFT and publishes it as an amendment of a submission: a persistence and cross-service constraint the prototype cannot express (c-165).
requirements.deltaNote: Today an amending notification is listed with every other notification, with a yellow 'Amending' tag; there are no tabs.

requirements.statement: Only the 'In progress' tab shows a count, in bold brackets, such as 'In progress (2)'; 'Draft' and 'Completed' show none, even when selected.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 counts only the notifications in flight; the count belongs to the tabs, which the 9 October afternoon ruling builds now, not to the blocked Summary cards.

requirements.statement: Under the tabs the cards sit under an h3 naming the tab: 'Notifications in progress', 'Draft notifications' or 'Completed notifications'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's subheading for each tab panel.

requirements.statement: The live animals list shows 8 notifications a page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's page size for every list; the 9 October afternoon ruling pages the reframed list 8 at a time.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page size comes from the listing: 25 from the animals backend (end-to-end) and 20 from the frontend stub (fit).

requirements.statement: A list of more than one page shows GOV.UK pagination with numbered page links, a 'Previous' link from page 2 and a 'Next' link before the last page; a list of one page, or no results, shows no pagination. This holds on the live animals list and on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 uses numbered pagination; today both lists have only Previous and Next. Plants takes the same paging in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today both lists use block-style pagination with only Previous and Next links and no page numbers.

requirements.statement: A page number below 1 or not a number shows page 1, and a page past the last shows the last page, on the live animals list as on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 clamps the page, so a stale or hand-typed page never shows an empty list; plants' list already does this.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the live animals list asked for a page past the last shows an empty page with 'Showing 0 of T Results' and only a Previous link; plants' list already clamps both ways (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-041, p3-042).

requirements.statement: The live animals list's page links keep the tab (unless 'In progress'), the sort (unless the default), the search text and every additional filter.
requirements.why: Because the real search and filters apply, a page link that dropped them would show a different, unfiltered list on page 2 (c-163).
requirements.deltaNote: Today Previous and Next keep the sort (unless the default) and the reference search; there are no tabs or filters to keep.

requirements.statement: The list shows no results count: the 'Showing 1 Result', 'Showing S to E of T Results', 'Showing N of T Results' and 'No Results' line goes, from the live animals list and from plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's category list shows no results count; DR1 only deferred its rewrite of the count; plants takes the same frame.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a small bold line above both lists' cards reads 'No Results', 'Showing 1 Result', 'Showing N of T Results' or 'Showing S to E of T Results' (Welsh twins on plants).

requirements.statement: A search or filter that matches nothing shows an empty list with no message: the 'No notifications found' line goes, from the live animals list and from plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 has no empty-state message on any list; plants takes the same frame.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a search with no match on either list replaces the results line with 'No notifications found' and shows no cards.

requirements.statement: A tab or list with no notifications shows an empty list with no message: the sentence 'You have not started any notifications in this session.' goes, from the live animals list and from plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 has no empty-state message; today's sentence also wrongly says the animals list is session-scoped. Plants' own decision d-068 quoted the sentence, but the 9 October afternoon ruling gives plants the same frame (c-notification-list-003).
requirements.deltaNote: Today a user with no notifications who is not searching sees 'You have not started any notifications in this session.' on both lists (Welsh 'Nid ydych wedi dechrau unrhyw hysbysiadau yn y sesiwn hon.' on plants).

requirements.statement: Each notification card on the live animals list and on plants' list is labelled for screen readers 'Notification <reference>' and has the reference as its h3.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's card names itself to assistive technology, and the 9 October afternoon ruling names the cards for screen readers in the reframed frame; the reference heading already exists on both lists.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each card on both lists is a GOV.UK summary card with the reference (or the journey id before one is issued) as its level-3 title, but no 'Notification <reference>' accessible name.

requirements.statement: A live animals card shows its facts in two rows: 'Commodity', 'Arrival date', 'Consignee' and 'Notification status', then the quantity, 'Origin', 'Consignor' and, when inspection is required, 'Inspection'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's card leads with what is coming, when, to whom and its status.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the card shows eight facts in three rows: Commodity, Origin, 'Arrival at destination'; Consignee, Consignor, Status; 'Date created', 'Date submitted'.

requirements.statement: The card labels the arrival date 'Arrival date', on the live animals list and on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label; DR1's own rename row was deferred, not judged; plants takes the same card layout.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the label is 'Arrival at destination' on the animals card and 'Arrival' on plants' card.

requirements.statement: The card labels the status 'Notification status', on the live animals list and on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label for the status fact; plants takes the same card layout.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the label is 'Status' on both cards.

requirements.statement: A live animals notification's card shows its quantity as 'Number of animals', from the notification's own count in the animals backend's record.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows how much is coming on every card; today no card shows a quantity, and the 9 October afternoon ruling takes the card's facts from the animals backend's record.

requirements.statement: The card shows no 'Date created' and no 'Date submitted', on the live animals list and on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's card has no dates other than arrival; today's 'Date submitted' is also blank on every card, submitted ones included, on both lists.
requirements.deltaNote: Today both cards show 'Date created' and 'Date submitted' (the latter blank in every end-to-end trace, and blank in plants' real mode because its backend returns no submitted date).

requirements.statement: The card writes the arrival date as the day, the full month name and the year, such as '21 June 2026', on the live animals list and on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's card writes the arrival date with the full month name, in its code and its render alike, and nothing overrides the prototype here (c-164).
requirements.deltaNote: Today both cards write the arrival date as day, short month name and year, such as '7 Nov 2026' (in English months even on the Welsh plants list).

requirements.statement: A card whose notification has no commodity, no arrival date or no quantity yet shows 'Not applicable' for that fact instead of a blank value, on the live animals list and on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 never shows an empty fact; today a draft card is mostly empty labels.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a field with no answer yet is shown with an empty value and no placeholder on both lists.

requirements.statement: The live animals card's commodity is the notification's commodity name.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names the commodity as the trader chose it; germinal products need the product type as well as the species (req-1738).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the card shows the commodity's common name for its code (a commodity chosen as Bos taurus shows 'Cow').

requirements.statement: A draft's status is a 'Draft' tag and an action-required notification's an 'Action required' tag, while 'Submitted' is plain styled text, not a tag; plants' card follows the same styles for Draft and Submitted and keeps its 'Late' tag.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 uses a tag only for statuses that ask something of the trader; plants mirrors the components (c-notification-list-004), and 'Action required' is animals only, because it rests on the ITAHC.
requirements.deltaNote: Today every status on both lists is a tag: Draft blue, Submitted green, Amending yellow (Deleted grey, never shown). The 'Completed' style is req-1739.

requirements.statement: A delayed notification shows a 'Delayed' tag on an error card with the reason for the delay; the prototype's placeholder text 'Error message' is not copied.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows delays on the list; its message is placeholder copy.
requirements.blockedBy: The authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sends post-submission outcomes (action required with its reason, inspection required, delayed, completed) back to the notification record; no delay status or reason reaches the service today.

requirements.statement: A notification the authorities have finished with shows the status 'Completed' and is listed in the 'Completed' tab.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 moves finished notifications out of the in-progress list; the completed status waits for a real source of completion.
requirements.blockedBy: The authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sends post-submission outcomes (action required with its reason, inspection required, delayed, completed) back to the notification record; no completed status reaches the service today.

requirements.statement: A notification chosen for inspection shows an extra 'Inspection' fact with a 'Required' tag at the end of the card's second row.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 warns the trader on the list that the consignment will be inspected.
requirements.blockedBy: The authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sends post-submission outcomes (action required with its reason, inspection required, delayed, completed) back to the notification record; no inspection decision reaches the service today.

requirements.statement: A live animals card keeps its status-driven actions, each named for screen readers with ' notification <reference>': a draft offers Resume, 'Copy as new' and Delete; a submitted notification offers View, Amend, 'Copy as new' and Delete; a notification being amended offers Resume, 'Copy as new', 'Cancel amendment' and Delete. Amend and 'Copy as new' stay link-styled buttons that post, in the same typeface as the links.
requirements.why: DR1 judged that the card keeps its status-driven links rather than DR1's flat 'Copy as new' and 'View', and that judgement wins over Design Release 2.1's same flat pair. Without it a trader could not resume a draft from the list.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-047, p3-050 and p3-052 (proven by trace-animals-fit-p2-037, p2-042 and p2-044): the card already offers these sets in this order, with visually hidden ' notification <reference>' text.

requirements.statement: A card in a status the real service does not have today (delayed or completed, and action required where it has no status-driven set of its own) offers 'Copy as new' then 'View', View opening the notification's review page.
requirements.why: DR1's judgement covers only the card links built today; for the new statuses nothing overrides Design Release 2.1, whose card offers 'Copy as new' and 'View'.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a notification in any status other than Draft, Submitted or Amending has no actions on its card.
requirements.blockedBy: The authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sends post-submission outcomes (action required with its reason, inspection required, delayed, completed) back to the notification record; until it does, no card is in these statuses.

requirements.statement: After an action that sends the trader back to the list with that action's flag on the redirect (such as a delete), the list shows a GOV.UK success notification banner with role alert, titled 'Success', carrying that action's message; plants' deletion banner takes the same 'Success' title.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 uses one success banner titled 'Success'; the message itself is set by the action. The 9 October ruling keeps the flag on the redirect (such as ?deleted=1) rather than a message held for the trader (c-252), and the afternoon ruling gives plants' banner the same title in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the banners are titled for the action: 'Notification deleted' with 'The notification has been deleted.' on both lists, and 'Notification copied' with 'A new draft notification has been created.' on the animals list (never reached).

requirements.statement: The success message is held for the trader and shown once, then cleared, rather than shown whenever the list's address carries a flag such as ?deleted=1.
requirements.why: The 2026-10-09 ruling drops moving the success banner to a message held for the trader and shown once (req-1087, inc-140 criteria 2 and 3): the flag on the redirect, such as ?deleted=1, stays, so the banner shows whenever the list is opened with it (c-252).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the banners show whenever the dashboard is opened with ?deleted=1 or ?copied=1, and that stays.

requirements.statement: The notification list's success banner, the deletion message included, does not dismiss itself on the live animals list or on plants' list: it stays until the trader leaves or reloads the page.
requirements.why: A message that disappears on a timer can vanish before a screen reader or a slow reader reaches it (WCAG 2.2.1); this accessibility duty overrides Design Release 2.1's 5-second auto-dismiss, and the 9 October afternoon ruling confirms it (c-006).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-062, repo-frontend-p3-065 and repo-plantsfrontend-p3-081: today's deletion banners are GOV.UK success banners announced as alerts, with no timer that dismisses them.

requirements.statement: The live animals list keeps its stale-action banner ('The notification has been updated' / 'This notification was updated since you opened it. Review the details and try again.') and its 'There is a problem' banner when a copy from the list fails.
requirements.why: Concurrency and failure handling are real constraints the prototype cannot express, so they stay although Design Release 2.1 shows neither.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-067 and repo-frontend-p3-066: the dashboard shows the stale-action banner with ?staleAction=1 and the 'There is a problem' banner with HTTP 500 after a failed copy.

requirements.statement: Every list string has a Welsh version, on the animals lists and on plants' list, marked as a machine draft that ships only after a translator signs it off under the Welsh Language Standards.
requirements.why: Both real services are bilingual and their dashboard Welsh is an unreviewed machine draft; Design Release 2.1's new strings need Welsh twins too.
requirements.deltaNote: Today every English dashboard key on both lists has a machine-drafted Welsh twin, not yet reviewed by a translator; plants' English dashboard copy is also marked provisional.

requirements.statement: The live animals list has no serious or critical WCAG 2 A or AA axe violations, empty or with cards, and does not scroll sideways at 1280px or at 769px wide; plants' list has no serious or critical WCAG 2 A or AA axe violations.
requirements.why: Both real lists meet this today and the reframed lists must keep meeting it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-118, p3-119, p3-108 and repo-plantsfrontend-p3-127: fit tests prove no serious or critical axe violations, and no sideways scroll on the animals list.

requirements.statement: The germinal products set's root in the animals frontend renders its own copy of the reframed list: the caption 'Dashboard', the h1 'Germinal products', the same search, sort, additional filters and tabs pointed at its own address, and a 'Create new' button that starts a germinal products notification in the germinal products set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives each category of animal notification its own list; the 9 October afternoon ruling builds the germinal list as the germinal set's own copy of the reframed live animals list (inc-141), instead of an INS germinal list.

requirements.statement: The live animals list shows only live animals notifications: a germinal products notification never appears on it, and a notification whose record holds no category counts as live animals.
requirements.why: A trader looking at one category must not see another's notifications; the animals backend stores each notification's category on its record, an absent category meaning live animals, and the reframed list reads that record.

requirements.statement: Deleted notifications never appear on any list or in a search.
requirements.why: A deleted notification is gone for the trader; both Design Release 2.1 and the real services leave it out.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p3-002, repo-frontend-p3-025 and repo-plantsfrontend-p3-044: the animals backend's list leaves out DELETED notifications, and both frontends filter them out.

requirements.statement: A newly started notification appears on the list straight away.
requirements.why: A trader must find their new draft on the list as soon as they have started it; the list reads the animals backend's own record, not an event-populated read model that lags writes.

requirements.statement: The animals backend's list API takes a search text and returns every notification whose reference number, commodity, consignee or consignor contains it, ignoring case and surrounding spaces, paged like any other list.

requirements.statement: The animals backend's list API sorts by creation date (newest or oldest first) and by arrival date, defaults to arrival date newest first, and breaks ties on a second key so no notification repeats or goes missing between pages.

conflicts.about: How the card writes the arrival date: '21/06/2026' or '21 June 2026'.

positions.says: The card shows the arrival date as dd/mm/yyyy with leading zeros, or the stored text when it cannot be read as a date.
Arrival dates on rendered cards read day, full month name and year, such as '21 June 2026'.
Today's card shows the chosen arrival day; the traces render it as day, short month name and year.

conflicts.outcome: The Design Release 2.1 card writes the arrival date as day, full month name and year, such as '21 June 2026'. The prototype's code and render agree: at 04a073b the card partial (app/views/partials/design-release-2.1/dashboard-notification-card.html) prints arrivalDateDisplay, which formatDashboardArrivalDate (app/routes.js:7201) builds from notification.arrivalDate; it only rewrites a d/m/yyyy value to dd/mm/yyyy and otherwise passes the stored text through. Every value the card receives is already 'D Month YYYY': the seed data in app/data/dashboard-notifications.js stores '21 June 2026', and submitted notifications store formatDateForDashboard(snapshot.arrivalDateAtPort) (app/routes.js:6883, 6989), which writes the full month name via formatDeclarationDate. So the dd/mm/yyyy branch is never reached on the card, and the rendered '21 June 2026' is what the prototype does. Today's short month name ('7 Nov 2026') changes to the full month name on the live animals card and, in the same increment, on plants' card; no DR1 judgement or real constraint overrides the prototype on this difference.

conflicts.outcome: A notification being amended is listed in the 'In progress' tab with today's yellow 'Amending' tag and its status-driven actions (Resume, Copy as new, Cancel amendment, Delete). The tabs otherwise follow Design Release 2.1 ('In progress' for submitted and action-required, 'Draft' for drafts, 'Completed' for completed). The prototype's fallback mapping of unknown statuses to the draft variant is set aside for amendments only, because an amendment is a persisted, already-submitted notification under change (status AMEND, which nothing moves back to DRAFT, re-submitted as NotificationSubmissionAmended and deleted as a submission), a lifecycle and cross-service constraint the prototype cannot express. The live animals dashboard has a back link to the overall dashboard at the mount root.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October afternoon ruling ranks first: every link Design Release 2.1 points at the overall dashboard goes to the set's own list, which is now the set's landing page, and the INS front door is reached through the service navigation as today. So no list carries a 'Back' link to the overall home. prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-019 is not overruled because it also backs the Alpha phase banner the list keeps.

conflicts.about: Which components build the list's search button, 'Additional filters' disclosure, date pickers and tabs: the prototype's custom markup or the GOV.UK and MoJ toolbox.

positions.says: The search button is custom markup (an inline SVG in a custom class), not a govuk-button.
'Additional filters' is a custom-styled native details element with a chevron image, not govuk-details.
The tabs are styled as govuk-tabs but rendered server-side, each a link that loads a new page.
inc-137's 'Additional filters' are built inside the one GET form from GOV.UK details, radios and a select, with an MoJ date picker on each end of the date range.
inc-135's tabs are MoJ sub navigation on the animals frontend's own list.
inc-136 is one GET form whose icon-only button is a real submit button.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October afternoon ruling ranks first: the list is built from the GOV.UK and MoJ toolbox, with no custom JavaScript. The search button is a real submit button that may show only an icon, with the accessible name 'Search'; 'Additional filters' is a GOV.UK details component with GOV.UK radios and select inside the one GET form; each end of the date range is an MoJ date picker; and the tabs are MoJ sub navigation links. The prototype's words, order and behaviour are kept; its custom markup is not copied. The trace claims are not overruled because they still back the button, the disclosure, its closed start and the tabs as links.

conflicts.about: Whether plants' list keeps the empty-list sentence 'You have not started any notifications in this session.' that its own decision d-068 quotes.

positions.says: d-068: a trader in a new session sees an empty list with the copy 'You have not started any notifications in this session.'
No list shows a message when it has no notifications; the list area is simply empty.
Plants' own list is reframed in the same increments with the same frame, card layout, tabs, paging, delete message and banner.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October afternoon ruling and the prototype rank above plants' own decision: plants' list takes the same frame as the live animals list, so its empty-list sentence goes. repo-plantsfrontend-p9-137 is not overruled because it still records that plants' listing is session-scoped, a user-model matter Sam parked, which this programme does not change.

conflicts.about: Whether plants' 'Submitted' status stays a green tag, as its own decision d-064 has it, or becomes plain text as on the live animals card.

positions.says: d-064: the status tags are Draft, Submitted, Amending and Deleted, coloured blue, green, yellow and grey.
A submitted notification shows the status as plain text 'Submitted'.
Plants mirrors structure, wording patterns, components and behaviour.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October afternoon ruling and the prototype rank above plants' own decision: plants' card mirrors the component, so 'Submitted' is plain styled text and 'Draft' a tag, as on the live animals card. repo-plantsfrontend-p9-128 is not overruled because it still backs plants' status vocabulary and its Draft and Amending tags, and its rule that check outcomes never change the importer-facing status.

conflicts.about: Whether plants' list can take the tabs and 8 a page in the same increments when its rows come from trade-imports-plants-backend, which takes no status filter or page size and is not one of the programme's repos.

positions.says: Plants' own list takes the same frame, card layout, tabs, paging, delete message and banner in the same increments.
A plants change that needs trade-imports-plants-backend is left out of the increment and recorded in deferred.md.
Plants' list is fetched page by page from the journey store with only the sort and reference filter applied server side.
The results range uses the backend's page size.

conflicts.outcome: Open: the ruling gives plants the tabs and the paging in the same increments, but splitting plants' list by status and paging it 8 at a time both need its list query to change, and that query is answered by trade-imports-plants-backend, which the ruling's own claim 51 leaves out of the programme.
conflicts.question: Do plants' tabs and 8-a-page paging wait with plants' search, sort and filters on trade-imports-plants-backend, or does the programme find a way to give them to plants now?
conflicts.default: The live animals and germinal products lists get the tabs and 8 a page now. Plants' list gets them in the same increment only if trade-imports-plants-backend's list already accepts a status filter and a page size; otherwise plants' tabs and 8-a-page wait with its search, sort and filters (deferred.md, blocked on the plants read model), and plants keeps one untabbed list paged as today while taking the rest of the frame now.
